input:
cd /hutian/story-wiki && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='Outline.md'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("- **C1 scale.**")
b=s.index("## 4. Paper structure")
new='''Rules (statistic and sentence; **all numbers are those of `PREANALYSIS.md` rev 2, cited and not copied here**):

- **C1 scale.** Per dataset and family, Δ = mean over pairs in the declared z-range of log Q_real − log Q_null against the dataset's own null. Equivalence (TOST-type) rule: "equivalent to the null" only if the whole 95% interval lies inside the stated margin, "differs" if wholly beyond, else "inconclusive at this size". "F collapses on z" is claimed only for the datasets equivalent to the null (count and share given). Exponents of log k\\* on log z and log N are reported as measured, not as "∝ z√N"; raw k\\*/N falls with N by the stated subsampling-slope rule.
- **C2 intent vs noise.** Primary: equal budget. Pair-specific P_flip of random deletion/outcome change at 0.5k\\*, k\\*, 2k\\* against the adversary's success, with F as the adversary's size in noise SEs; ρ_q only where random reaches q, with the share of pairs where it does; "far below noise" by the note's per-stratum rule.
- **C3 survival.** CI-separated pairs under the published-view definition (sensitivity: gap CI excludes 0) and the top-10 relations: fraction with k\\* > b in SE and √N units, and in absolute count and %-of-N (headline), P_flip as the noise reference; no threshold.
- **C4 design vs statistics.** Δ as in C1 per member; for a matched contrast the difference of Δ by joint cluster bootstrap; "design difference" only if the interval of the difference lies beyond the margin; M = 6 intervals are said to be coarse.
- **C5 predictive rule.** log k\\* regression, held-out unit = dataset; a design term is tested only where a design has ≥ 2 units (judges, seasons, crowd slices), crowd-55k and expert-MT-Bench alone have none; "helps" iff the paired held-out squared-error difference has an interval excluding 0, units counted; else "no evidence". "Rule transfers" is described by held-out error against intercept-only and log-z-only references, without a tuned threshold.
- **C6 search.** First-order accuracy and tightness by the note's rules on the small real anchors (the LP relaxation is a lower-bound *candidate*, labelled so, a certificate only where it coincides with exhaustive enumeration), and at scale by stronger independent search and planted instances.

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace("No margin was tuned on a real-data summary. Any rule changed after real results is reported as a deviation.","No margin was tuned on a real-data summary; the note was revised once (rev 2, after a review of it and before results were read into the story) and the paper says so. Any rule changed after real results is reported as a deviation.")
s=s.replace("# Outline (revision 3, after review 1 and the calibration)","# Outline (revision 4, rules cite PREANALYSIS.md rev 2)")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add -A; git -c user.name=story-repo -c user.email=s@x commit -qm "Outline rev 4: decision rules cite PREANALYSIS rev 2 instead of copying margins"; timeout 120 git push -q origin HEAD:main 2>&1|tail -2

shown.message:
I updated the Outline to revision 4 and pushed it to the wiki. The rules in §3a now cite `experiment-repo`'s `PREANALYSIS.md` rev 2 instead of copying its numbers. That note changed the equivalence margin and compares each dataset with its own null. The outline now records the note's rev 2 changes to the C1, C2, C4, C5 and C6 rules. It also says the note was revised once, which the paper must state.

I did not change the claims. The first result tables in `experiment-repo` (Arena 55k, MT-Bench, early NBA seasons) show real-data Q close to the null. They are too partial to change any claim, so I will revisit the outline when the core batch completes.

I haven't read the changed Brief (6 revisions, last edit 04:28 UTC). I assume it is the correction I asked for in `idea-repo`#5, but I haven't checked.
